facts.text: Ashford received its charter in 1714, growing from a rural farm community into the suburban town it is today.
The town hosts Connecticut’s largest Boy Scout camp, June Norcross Webster, and Paul Newman's Hole in the Wall Gang Camp for children.
Yale-Myers Forest spans Ashford, serving Yale School of Forestry research and sheltering the towering Ashford Oak, an eight‑meter‑circumference red oak.
Mount Hope River runs north‑south through the town, while Bigelow Brook borders Eastford, and lakes like Ashford Lake and Lake Chaffee dot the landscape.
Natchaug and Nipmuck State Forests extend into Ashford, with the Natchaug and Nipmuck Trails winding through its forests.
Joshua's Tract Conservation and Historic Trust protects several nature preserves across Ashford, safeguarding local wildlife and habitats.
